text:
5 A search of a person in public should be completed as soon as possible.

6 A person may be detained under a stop and search power at a place other than where the
person was first detained, only if that place, be it a police station or elsewhere, is nearby.
Such a place should be located within a reasonable travelling distance using whatever
Codes of practice – Code A Exercise by police of officers statutory powers of stop and search
24
A
mode of travel (on foot or by car) is appropriate. This applies to all searches under stop
and search powers, whether or not they involve the removal of clothing or exposure of
intimate parts of the body (see paragraphs 3.6 and 3.7) or take place in or out of public
view. It means, for example, that a search under the stop and search power in section 23
of the Misuse of Drugs Act 1971 which involves the compulsory removal of more than a
person’s outer coat, jacket or gloves cannot be carried out unless a place which is both
nearby the place they were first detained and out of public view, is available. If a search
involves exposure of intimate parts of the body and a police station is not nearby,
particular care must be taken to ensure that the location is suitable in that it enables the
search to be conducted in accordance with the requirements of paragraph 11 of Annex A
to Code C.
